reply_text:
I found two issues in `main...receipt-lines` (`a6c40d4`):

1. **[P1] Printed prices are 100× too high** — `receipt/render.py:2`  
   `format_money()` formats integer cents directly as dollars. `format_money(1299)` returns **`$1299.00`**, not `$12.99`; two $4.50 coffees print as `$900.00`. Convert cents to dollars before formatting. Add literal expected-value tests—the current render test compares against the same faulty formatter, so it passes.

2. **[P2] The right-alignment helper isn’t used by the renderer** — `receipt/render.py:7`  
   `render_line()` still pads only the name to 20 characters rather than using `layout.align()`. Amounts of different lengths end in different columns instead of at the 32-character edge. Route rendered lines through the alignment helper and test differing amount lengths through `render_line()`.

**Validation:** All 3 existing tests pass; direct output checks reproduce both issues. No files changed. I’d fix the currency formatting before merging.
